source_review.notes: Checked current RISC-V base and compressed specifications, the RISC-V opcode repository, GNU assembler and LLVM machine-code documentation, Arm and Intel architecture manuals, and the WebAssembly binary instruction specification. All eight cited authoritative URLs returned HTTP 200. One stale LLVM MC overview URL returned 404 during research and was excluded in favor of the current llvm-mc reference.

evidence: Checked byte sequence, profile-dependent decode/encode, bit slice, mask/match, legality, length, immediate, displacement, relocation and canonicalization notation.
Verified semantic instruction, assembly spelling, encoded word and increasing-address byte sequence are distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation treats decode as a partial profile-dependent function and states bit-zero and byte-order conventions explicitly.

evidence: Recomputed R-format add word 0x002081b3 and I-format addi word 0xff830293 from opcode, register and function fields.
Recomputed 0xff8 sign extension as -8, little-endian bytes b3812000 and 930283ff, and signed 12-bit range -2048 through 2047.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic Python snippet reproduced both expected round trips and the unsupported-opcode rejection.

evidence: Re-derived decode-after-encode semantic equality modulo documented alias normalization.
Checked the mask/match overlap criterion and inverse obligations for immediate fragment assembly, extension and scaling.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic arguments cover encoding structure and collision reasoning, not complete semantics or a full ISA decoder proof.

evidence: Reviewed truncated buffers, page/cache crossings, variable lengths, alignment, boundary registers/immediates, scattered fields, scaling, reserved bits and illegal near misses.
Reviewed disabled extensions, cross-extension collisions, malformed bytes, relocation overflow, split pairs, relaxation, aliases, speculative decode and errata.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Length, bit numbering, byte order, field extraction, legality, relocation and processor-trap boundaries receive separate treatment.

evidence: Checked unique length, full pattern tests, collision freedom, register legality, immediate inversion, range rejection and endian mapping.
Checked canonicalization, relocation, toolchain/profile agreement, precise illegal traps, independence and lifecycle binding across fifteen obligations.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariant set prevents valid-looking disassembly or a few round trips from standing in for complete accepted-language control.

evidence: Reviewed fifteen length, bit-number, pattern, collision, register, immediate, range, endian, legality, canonical, relocation, toolchain, processor, independence and lifecycle obligations.
Constructed counterexamples for mnemonic-uniquely-identifies-bytes, little-endian-reverses-fields, reserved-means-no-op, truncation-is-safe and round-trip-proves-correctness claims.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies proof obligations and bounded examples, not formal verification of RISC-V, Arm, Intel, WebAssembly, GNU Binutils, LLVM or hardware.

evidence: Audited uses of legal, illegal, reserved, unsupported, canonical, sound, deterministic, aligned, independent and verified.
Confirmed normative encodings, assembler choices, linker transformations, decoder implementations and processor effects remain separate.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The executable subset is explicitly not labeled as a complete RISC-V decoder or conformance proof.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CA-013/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, Python toolchain and environment for two round trips and one rejection.
Reviewed required specification, opcode-registry, assembler, linker, disassembler, executable-model, RTL, negative-space, binary-corpus, hardware and errata evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing snippet establishes two 32-bit field mappings only; it provides no evidence for compressed formats, relocation, full decoding, processor traps or silicon.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed instruction encoding as a profile-dependent, deterministic mapping among semantic instructions, fields, words and addressed bytes with explicit illegal space.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including length detection, masks/matches, collision checks, immediates, register constraints, byte order, alignment, extension allocation, aliases, canonicalization, object attributes, relocations, relaxation, decoder security and lifecycle governance. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from representations and bit conventions through decode, toolchain and processor evidence, followed by fifteen obligations, fifteen trade-offs, twenty-six misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external ISA academic, RISC-V, Arm, Intel or WebAssembly maintainer, opcode-registry steward, compiler or binary-tools engineer, RTL or formal-verification specialist, security assessor, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
